subject.title: fix(gmail): keep gmail watch secrets out of process argv

question: Should OpenClaw require compatible gogcli file-secret support and full Gmail runner coverage before accepting this argv-secret fix?
rationale: The branch changes a live external CLI contract and secret boundary, and automation cannot decide whether maintainers want dependency coordination, a narrower supported-flags mitigation, or a replacement branch.

options.title: Require dependency-backed full fix
options.body: Wait for compatible gogcli file-secret flags or capability detection, cover both runner paths, and require cleanup-safe implementation plus inspectable proof before merge.

options.title: Keep current gog contract for now
options.body: Do not switch OpenClaw to file-secret flags until gogcli support is released; accept only mitigations that preserve existing watcher startup behavior.

options.title: Pause or replace this branch
options.body: Close or supersede this PR if maintainers want the security fix to arrive as a coordinated replacement with dependency and proof handled together.

recommendation.title: Require dependency-backed full fix
recommendation.body: Wait for compatible gogcli file-secret flags or capability detection, cover both runner paths, and require cleanup-safe implementation plus inspectable proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This account introduced the Gmail hooks surface and is the strongest available owner signal for the shared helper and current maintainer decision.
